This pull request enhances the vaccination-related APIs by improving data retrieval and response handling. Key changes include:

## 🚘 What kind of work?

- 이전에 구성된 화면을 점검하면서 일부 화면을 변경하였습니다.
- more 버튼의 세부 기능을 구현하였습니다.
- Diary 화면을 생성하였습니다.

## ✈️ Changes

- MagicalScreen의 동영상이 안드로이드 화면에서는 컨트롤러가 보이는 문제로 nativeControls={false} 옵션을 추가했습니다.
- 제거된 Onboarding1Screen 코드를 복구하고 이전의 Onboarding1Screen 코드는 OnboardingScreen 파일로 변경했습니다.
- more 버튼의 SlidingMenu, DeleteConfirmModal, TextInputConfirmModal를 컴포넌트로 생성하였습니다.
- react-native-calendars를 이용해서 DiaryScreen을 생성하였습니다.
  - DiaryHeader: Diary와 more 버튼이 위치하는 상단 헤더입니다.
  - CustomDayComponent: 요일별, 선택 시 등의 날짜 색상을 변경합니다.

### Descrição
<!-- Descreva brevemente o que esse Pull Request faz. -->
Este Pull Request acompanha a funcionalidade de movimentação do jogador dentro das masmorras e a sua geração procedural, isto é, criação única e aleatória de salas dentro de uma masmorra.

- Cada Sala individual possui uma Semente de Geração, cujo é utilizada para estabelecer a aleatoriedade de conexão com outras salas adjacentes;
- Cada Masmorra possui uma Semente de Geração formada por:
   - `4 Dígitos Numéricos`-`Nickname e Nome da Masmorra Criptografada`-`Hash aleatório de 10 dígitos`
- O jogador se move pelas salas através da montagem de uma matriz, consultando as salas adjacentes a cada movimentação;
- O jogador não pode entrar em masmorras em que não derrotou o chefe da masmorra anterior.

## Proposed changes

There are lots of examples in `example/ck_tile` folder. However, there are some problems with them. 
1. These examples are used as both examples and smoke tests of ck tile. 
2. These examples (smoke tests) are not built by CI. Without the CI check, some ck tile PRs were merged into develop even these tests failed. 

In this PR, 
1. we migrated the existing smoke tests from `example/ck_tile` to `test/ck_tile`

Creating Python Programs
Part 1:
Write a program that calculates the total amount of a meal purchased at a restaurant. The program should ask the user to enter the charge for the food and then calculate the amounts with an 18 percent tip and 7 percent sales tax. Display each of these amounts and the total price.

Part 2:
Many people keep time using a 24-hour clock (11 is 11am and 23 is 11pm, 0 is midnight). If it is currently 13 and you set your alarm to go off in 50 hours, it will be 15 (3pm). Write a Python program to solve the general version of the above problem. Ask the user for the time now (in hours) and then ask for the number of hours to wait for the alarm. Your program should output what the time will be on a 24-hour clock when the alarm goes off.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a complete Flutter-based alternative UX that provides the same functionality as the Python Gamatrix web application while reading from the data store JSON files.

## 🎯 Implementation Overview

A standalone Flutter application (`flutter_gamatrix/`) that offers:

- **Cross-platform support**: Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, Linux
- **Data store integration**: Reads Gamatrix JSON data store files directly
- **Feature parity**: All filtering and viewing options from the web interface
- **Mobile-optimized UI**: Modern Material Design with dark theme matching the original

## 📁 Project Structure

```
flutter_gamatrix/
├── lib/
│   ├── main.dart                    # App entry point with dark theme
│   ├── models/data_models.dart      # Dart classes mirroring Python dataclasses
│   ├── services/data_store_service.dart # JSON ingestion and filtering
│   ├── screens/                     # UI screens (home, game list, game grid)
│   └── widgets/game_card.dart       # Reusable game card component
├── test/                            # Unit tests for data models
├── sample_data_store.json           # Demo data with 10 games, 3 users
├── pubspec.yaml                     # Flutter dependencies and configuration
└── README.md                        # Complete setup and usage documentation
```

## ✨ Key Features

### Data Integration
- **JSON Data Store Support**: Reads data store files created by the Python application
- **Sample Data**: Includes demo data for testing without Python setup
- **File Picker**: Load data store files from device storage
- **Persistent Storage**: Remembers last used data store file

### User Interface
- **Home Screen**: User selection, filtering options, and view mode selection
- **Game List View**: Detailed cards with installation status, search functionality
- **Game Grid View**: Ownership matrix with color-coded cells (green=owns, red=doesn't own)
- **Search**: Filter games by title or platform across all views

### Filtering Options (matching Python version)
- **User Selection**: Multi-user game library comparison
- **Installed Only**: Show games installed by all selected users
- **Single-player Toggle**: Include/exclude single-player games
- **Exclusive Ownership**: Games owned only by selected users
- **Platform Exclusions**: Filter out specific platforms (Steam, GOG, Epic, etc.)
- **Random Selection**: Pick one random game from filtered results

## 🎨 UI/UX Design

- **Dark Theme**: Matches original Gamatrix web interface (rgb(50,50,50) background)
- **Material Design**: Modern, responsive Flutter components
- **Expandable Cards**: Detailed game information with ownership status
- **Color Coding**: Visual indicators for ownership and installation status
- **Search Integration**: Real-time filtering across game collections

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

### Data Models
```dart
class GameData {
  final String releaseKey;
  final String title;
  final List<String> platforms;
  final List<int> owners;
  final List<int> installed;
  final bool multiplayer;
  // ... mirrors Python GameData exactly
}
```

### Service Layer
- **DataStoreService**: Handles JSON parsing, game filtering, and random selection
- **Error Handling**: Graceful fallbacks when data store files are invalid
- **Performance**: Efficient filtering algorithms for large game collections

## 📱 Installation & Usage

1. **Install Flutter SDK**: Follow [Flutter installation guide](https://docs.flutter.dev/get-started/install)
2. **Navigate to app**: `cd flutter_gamatrix`
3. **Install dependencies**: `flutter pub get`
4. **Run application**: `flutter run`
5. **Load data**: Use folder icon to select data store JSON file or demo with included sample

## 🧪 Testing

- **Unit Tests**: Data model serialization/deserialization validation
- **Widget Tests**: Basic app smoke tests
- **Sample Data**: Comprehensive test data with multiple users and games

## 📝 Documentation

- **Flutter README**: Complete setup, usage, and troubleshooting guide
- **Updated Main README**: Added Flutter section with quick start instructions
- **Code Comments**: Detailed documentation throughout the codebase

## 🔄 Compatibility

- **No Python Changes**: Existing Gamatrix functionality remains unchanged
- **Data Store Format**: Uses existing JSON data store structure
- **Feature Complete**: All web interface capabilities available in Flutter app

Fixes #7.

This pull request updates the `ExportVaccinationResultsExcelFileAsync` method in the `ExportFileService` class to enhance the exported Excel file with additional fields related to vaccination observations and reactions. It also refactors the order of existing columns and simplifies conditional logic for populating cell values.

### Enhancements to Excel Export:

* Added new columns to the Excel file for detailed vaccination observation data, including `ReactionStartTime`, `ReactionType`, `SeverityLevel`, `ImmediateReaction`, `Intervention`, `ObservationEndTime`, `ObservationStartTime`, and `ObservedBy`. These columns provide more comprehensive information about post-vaccination reactions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8a5a0e9f275aa147394f857237e5cc1badd2c25c18000c1b8456fff92cb1d866L213-R228) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8a5a0e9f275aa147394f857237e5cc1badd2c25c18000c1b8456fff92cb1d866L257-R283)
* Updated the range for the title row to accommodate the newly added columns, ensuring proper styling for the expanded set of headers.

### Refactoring and Simplification:

* Swapped the order of the `Notes` and `ObservationNotes` columns in the header row for better organization and consistency.
* Simplified conditional logic for populating cell values, using the null-coalescing operator (`??`) to handle cases where observation data may be missing.

### Code Cleanup:

* Removed unnecessary blank lines and streamlined the layout of the method for improved readability.Rearranged and added new columns in the Excel worksheet headers, including "ReactionStartTime," "ReactionType," "SeverityLevel," "ImmediateReaction," "Intervention," "ObservationEndTime," "ObservationStartTime," and "ObservedBy." Adjusted the title range accordingly.

Modified data population logic for "Notes" and "ObservationNotes" fields to pull from the appropriate objects, enhancing the detail of health observation data.

author: vimly-ai
body:
## Problem
After restoring the repository to the June 14th state, Netlify is failing to deploy with the error:
```
"Could not resolve '../components/ui/contact' from 'src/pages/contact.astro'"
```

This is the same import issue that was previously fixed in PR #6, where the contact.astro page was trying to import a component without the required .astro file extension.

## Solution
Updated the import statement in `src/pages/contact.astro` from:
```javascript
import Contact from '../components/ui/contact';
```

to:
```javascript
import Contact from '../components/ui/contact.astro';
```

## Testing
- ✅ Verified that the contact component exists at `src/components/ui/contact.astro`
- ✅ Confirmed the import path is correct with the .astro extension
- ✅ This fix follows Astro's requirement for explicit file extensions in imports

## Impact
This resolves the Netlify build failure and allows successful deployment of the restored June 14th codebase.

Fixes the "Could not resolve '../components/ui/contact'" error that was preventing successful deployment.

body:
## Pull Request: Lambda createEvent funcional + pruebas unitarias

### Descripción

Este PR agrega la función Lambda `createEvent` completamente funcional, con integración a RDS (PostgreSQL) y Kinesis, junto con pruebas unitarias.

### Cambios principales

- Inserción de eventos en PostgreSQL usando el paquete `pg`.
- Envío de eventos a un stream de Kinesis (`event-stream`).
- Manejo de errores y logs en CloudWatch.
- Infraestructura: Lambda en subred privada con acceso a RDS y Kinesis mediante NAT Gateway.
- Pruebas unitarias con Jest, incluyendo mocks de `pg` y `aws-sdk`.
- Configuración de Jest en `package.json`.

body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the virtualization implementation, including enhancements to the `VirtualList` component, new functionality for intersection observers, and the addition of a resize observer demonstration. It also updates the repository documentation and styling to improve usability and clarity.

### Virtualization Enhancements:
1. **Core VirtualList Component**: 
   - Added `VirtualList` class to handle virtualized rendering, intersection observers, and element recycling. Features include a pool for element reuse, methods for handling top and bottom observers, and CSS transformations for smooth transitions. (`5-virtualisation/5-1-skeleton/begin/virtual-list.js`, [5-virtualisation/5-1-skeleton/begin/virtual-list.jsR1-R203](diffhunk://#diff-091300a1013a520ea6d06594a89f5a800dad77790595b63329a382ea8e529536R1-R203))
   - Defined methods for updating data and absolute positioning of elements during recycling. (`5-virtualisation/5-1-skeleton/begin/virtual-list.js`, [5-virtualisation/5-1-skeleton/begin/virtual-list.jsR1-R203](diffhunk://#diff-091300a1013a520ea6d06594a89f5a800dad77790595b63329a382ea8e529536R1-R203))

2. **Observer Utility**:
   - Introduced `intersectionObserver` utility function to simplify observer registration with configurable options. (`utils/observer.js`, [utils/observer.jsR1-R20](diffhunk://#diff-316f462618100479c0615d982c3fe248fb597ffbf1c578c7e83a055fcea4389cR1-R20))

3. **Styling Updates**:
   - CSS changes to support virtualization, including relative positioning for containers and absolute positioning for cards. (`5-virtualisation/5-1-skeleton/begin/virtualisation.css`, [5-virtualisation/5-1-skeleton/begin/virtualisation.cssR1-R20](diffhunk://#diff-8b384ebe251050e4977447d286d6bdf3c6bf823bb15fc333bca97284b4ea633aR1-R20))
   - Updated observer styles for visual clarity. (`styles/index.css`, [styles/index.cssR33-R48](diffhunk://#diff-25686218953cfea3103c15d0a839fe3c6c2ccb91543c6ff7478007640f1ba910R33-R48))

### Resize Observer Demonstration:
- Added a new example using `ResizeObserver` to dynamically adjust element styles based on size changes. (`4-resize-observer/end/index.html`, [4-resize-observer/end/index.htmlR1-R82](diffhunk://#diff-346a178aaf8163851c7194b17224932a7ed2942abb452b0a099187a091772b3bR1-R82))

### Repository Documentation:
- Updated `README.md` with detailed instructions on using branches for exercises and solutions in the workshop. (`README.md`, [README.mdL1-R25](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L1-R25))

Below is a list of all new features, APIs, and bug fixes.

Read the [React 19.2 release post](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/01/react-19-2) for more information.

##### New React Features

- [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity): A new API to hide and restore the UI and internal state of its children.
- [`useEffectEvent`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent) is a React Hook that lets you extract non-reactive logic into an [Effect Event](https://react.dev/learn/separating-events-from-effects#declaring-an-effect-event).
- [`cacheSignal`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cacheSignal) (for RSCs) lets your know when the `cache()` lifetime is over.
- [React Performance tracks](https://react.dev/reference/dev-tools/react-performance-tracks) appear on the Performance panel’s timeline in your browser developer tools

##### New React DOM Features

- Added resume APIs for partial pre-rendering with Web Streams:
  - [`resume`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/server/resume): to resume a prerender to a stream.
  - [`resumeAndPrerender`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/static/resumeAndPrerender): to resume a prerender to HTML.
- Added resume APIs for partial pre-rendering with Node Streams:
  - [`resumeToPipeableStream`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/server/resumeToPipeableStream): to resume a prerender to a stream.
  - [`resumeAndPrerenderToNodeStream`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/static/resumeAndPrerenderToNodeStream): to resume a prerender to HTML.
- Updated [`prerender`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/static/prerender) APIs to return a `postponed` state that can be passed to the `resume` APIs.

##### Notable changes

- React DOM now batches suspense boundary reveals, matching the behavior of client side rendering. This change is especially noticeable when animating the reveal of Suspense boundaries e.g. with the upcoming `<ViewTransition>` Component. React will batch as much reveals as possible before the first paint while trying to hit popular first-contentful paint metrics.
- Add Node Web Streams (`prerender`, `renderToReadableStream`) to server-side-rendering APIs for Node.js

- adds `SOAPEnvelope.createName(String, String): Name` method
- does not allow null arguments in `SOAPFault.createFault(String, String)`
- extends `SOAPConnection` to implement `java.io.Autocloseable`
- adds API to allow setting timeouts for set timeout for `SOAPConnection.call`
- drops all references to JAXM
- drops the search through Java SE installation in the implementation lookup
- removes deprecated `SOAPElementFactory`

author: ranarino
body:
**Description:**

This PR introduces the foundational architecture and design for the project. The key updates are as follows:

### 1. Architecture Decision
*   **Microservices Architecture:** We have adopted a full microservices architecture to ensure future scalability and maintainability.
*   **Service Definition:** Initial core services have been defined, including Knowledge, Canvas, Chat, Vector, and Activity services.

### 2. Database and Entity Design
*   The initial database schemas for the core microservices have been designed.
*   Key data entities, such as `SPACES` for the Knowledge Service, have been defined.

### 3. Frontend Requirements
*   Detailed functional requirements for the main user interfaces have been specified, including:
    *   Space list and gallery views with filtering and search.
    *   The main "Space" view with resizable panels.
    *   Features like soft-delete, custom cover images, and in-place editing.
    *   An annotation mode for interacting with AI-generated content.

### 4. Research & Documentation
*   A review of relevant academic research on information visualization has been added to inform the UI/UX design.
*   Added presentation slides (`slide.pdf`) to the documentation.

author: akdotcom
body:
Implemented a two-player hexagon tile game with the following features:

- Basic HTML structure and CSS styling.
- JavaScript for game logic:
  - Hexagonal tile representation with edges (blank or triangle).
  - Axial coordinates for hex grid management.
  - Correct neighbor detection and edge matching for tile placement.
  - Player turns, tile selection, and placement on the board.
  - Generation of 14 unique tiles per player (randomized).
  - Game end condition (both players out of tiles).
  - Scoring based on connected triangles of the same player's color.
  - Reset game functionality.
- Visuals:
  - Tiles styled as hexagons using CSS `clip-path`.
  - Basic visual indicators for tile edges.

Known limitations:
- The CSS for laying out the hexagonal grid cells themselves is basic and may require JavaScript-assisted positioning or more advanced CSS for a visually perfect grid.
- Tile edge indicators are positioned approximately.
- Tile generation is random and could be improved for more controlled sets.

This commit provides a functional core for the game.

## About the PR
This implements the SmartFridge, allowing chemists or botanists to index large amounts of chemicals or produce in a vending machine-like interface for others to take from.

## Why / Balance
The SmartFridge does not serve its purpose as a storage device well when used as a normal locker, as it is bulkier and cannot be constructed. Augmenting its storage capability with a user interface better suited to indexing mass amounts of items allows it to fulfill a niche that other storage devices cannot handle.

This also makes playstyles for chemists dosing out individual bottles and pill canisters to doctors more viable with actual mechanical support.

## Technical details
- genercise the DumpableSystem to not be hardcoded to disposal units and tables
- new SmartFridge component and associated system & user interface

author: tannerdino
body:
Ash has said in the past that a command like obj_adddelayed, is a more recent command. They currently use it for firemaking.

I think something like inv_dropitem_delayed has to have existed in 2004 though. In old videos, the arrows will land where the target *used* to be... This means that they wouldve needed to store the coord some how (with no local vars!). `obj_add` also takes namedobj, so they would've needed to have a way to change the ammo obj to namedobj (confident they did not do this).

The big nail in the coffin is when I was implementing magic shortbow spec. Theres a p_delay(0) in between the two arrows... since our current arrow dropping relies on world_delay, there will be certain scenarios where you want to obj_add instantly after the p_delay. With two arrows dropping at potentially different times, this can get messy real quick.

author: chonknick
body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the `chonkie` library, including a version bump, dependency adjustments, and a major shift in the default tokenizer across multiple chunker classes and the tokenizer implementation. These changes aim to simplify the codebase and improve compatibility.

### Dependency Updates:
* Updated the library version in `pyproject.toml` from `1.0.10` to `1.1.0`.
* Removed `tokenizers` from required dependencies and added it as an optional dependency under `tokenizers` and `all`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711L48-R48) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711R60-R71) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711R89-L92)

### Default Tokenizer Changes:
* Changed the default tokenizer from `"gpt2"` to `"character"` in the following chunker classes: `CodeChunker`, `RecursiveChunker`, `SentenceChunker`, `SlumberChunker`, and `TokenChunker`. body:
This pull request introduces significant changes to the `apps/frontend` project, including the implementation of authentication flows, internationalization, and app structure updates. Key updates include the addition of authentication-related screens, hooks, and services, the integration of i18n for localization, and the migration to `expo-router` for navigation. Below is a categorized summary of the most important changes:

### Authentication Features
* Added `useAuth` hook to manage user authentication state and provide login/logout functionality (`apps/frontend/hooks/useAuth.ts`).
* Implemented `LoginScreen` with form validation using `react-hook-form` and `zod`, and integrated the `AuthService` for API calls (`apps/frontend/app/signin.tsx`).
* Created `AuthService` to handle login requests via a centralized API service (`apps/frontend/services/authService.ts`).

### App Structure and Navigation
* Replaced `App.tsx` with a new `expo-router` entry point and restructured the app layout with `RootLayout` and `AppLayout` components for authenticated and unauthenticated flows (`apps/frontend/app/_layout.tsx`, `apps/frontend/app/(authenticated)/_layout.tsx`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6188fc0060a8d30edc4a9ce065e4e4fa0ee5e0fc65651662416836f42ec90691R1-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e482756682fcdc8f35b57145e9167e46d971b194527b4c42125dd529f14f51a4R1-R12)
* Added `WelcomeScreen` for onboarding users with options to sign in or sign up (`apps/frontend/app/index.tsx`).

### Localization (i18n)
* Integrated `i18next` with English and Indonesian translations for the app's text content (`apps/frontend/i18n/index.ts`, `apps/frontend/i18n/resources/en/translation.json`, `apps/frontend/i18n/resources/id/translation.json`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3371f9b1635cbf9b6471c269c399d178872d0be293175eb932389c85fc0cb3edR1-R26) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-779bca09fb4be2d3dac5031b4fd93b65397697a97813582404392d0857365083R1-R25) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8181cbbaf4e331d6e62ff087e64be78f9a4ebd6b490a976b305fd12d20869930R1-R25)

### API and State Management
* Added a global `useApi` hook to handle API calls with loading, error, and result states (`apps/frontend/hooks/useApi.ts`).
* Implemented `useApp` hook to manage app-level state such as hydration and onboarding status (`apps/frontend/hooks/useApp.ts`).
* Configured a centralized Axios instance for API requests with interceptors for request and response handling (`apps/frontend/lib/api.ts`).

### Dependency Updates
* Added new dependencies for form handling (`react-hook-form`, `zod`), localization (`i18next`, `react-i18next`), navigation (`expo-router`), and state management (`zustand`) (`apps/frontend/package.json`).

body:
## 🔧 Fix: Accessibility Permission Detection Issues

### Problem
Even after users granted accessibility permissions in System Preferences, WhisperNode continued to show "Accessibility Permissions Required" and failed to detect the granted permissions. This prevented users from using hotkey functionality.

### Root Cause
- Timing issues with macOS permission detection
- Insufficient debugging information for troubleshooting
- No recovery mechanisms when permissions weren't detected properly
- Lack of robust permission refresh functionality

### Solution
Enhanced the `PermissionHelper` class with comprehensive improvements:

#### 🚀 Key Enhancements

**1. Enhanced Permission Debugging**
- Added detailed logging for permission status, bundle ID, and process name
- Improved visibility into permission check results
- Better tracking of permission state changes

**2. Robust Permission Refresh Mechanism**
- Multiple permission checks with timing delays to handle macOS system delays
- Secondary validation to catch inconsistent permission states
- Automatic retry logic for edge cases

**3. Improved User Experience**
- Enhanced "Check Again" functionality with better reliability
- New "Help" button with detailed troubleshooting steps
- "Restart App" option when permissions still aren't detected
- Better error messages with specific guidance

**4. Advanced Troubleshooting Support**
- Comprehensive help dialog with step-by-step instructions
- Bundle ID display for verification
- Manual app restart functionality
- Enhanced permission guidance with common solutions

### 📁 Files Changed
- `Sources/WhisperNode/Utils/PermissionHelper.swift` - Enhanced permission detection and troubleshooting
- `Sources/WhisperNode/UI/ShortcutTab.swift` - Fixed SwiftUI compatibility issue

### 🧪 Testing Results
- ✅ Permission detection now works reliably after granting permissions
- ✅ Enhanced debugging provides clear visibility into permission status
- ✅ "Check Again" button successfully refreshes permission state
- ✅ Help system guides users through troubleshooting steps
- ✅ Hotkey functionality works immediately after permission detection
- ✅ No app restart required when permissions are granted

### 🔍 Technical Details

**Enhanced Permission Checking:**
```swift
// Added detailed debugging
Self.logger.debug("Accessibility permission check: \(result ? "GRANTED" : "DENIED")")
Self.logger.debug("Bundle identifier: \(Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier ?? "unknown")")
Self.logger.debug("Process name: \(ProcessInfo.processInfo.processName)")
```

**Robust Refresh Mechanism:**
```swift
// Multiple checks with timing delays
let check1 = checkPermissionsQuietly()
DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.1) { [weak self] in
    let check2 = self?.checkPermissionsQuietly() ?? false
    if check1 != check2 {
        self?.updatePermissionStatus()
    }
}
```

### 🎯 User Impact
- **Before**: Users had to restart the app after granting permissions
- **After**: Permissions are detected immediately with enhanced troubleshooting
- **Improved**: Clear guidance when issues occur with step-by-step solutions
- **Enhanced**: Better debugging for future permission-related issues

### 📋 Validation Steps
1. Install app and verify permission banner appears
2. Grant accessibility permissions in System Preferences
3. Use "Check Again" button to refresh status
4. Verify permission banner disappears and hotkeys work
5. Test help system and troubleshooting guidance

### 🔗 Related Issues
Resolves accessibility permission detection issues that prevented hotkey functionality from working after permissions were granted.

---

**Testing Environment:**
- macOS with accessibility permissions
- Debug build with ad-hoc signing
- Verified with remove/re-add permission workflow

---

## Summary

This PR refactors the controller architecture to fix poor naming and mixed responsibilities by splitting the monolithic `HttpController` into three properly named, single-responsibility controllers.

### Problems Solved
- **Poor naming**: `HttpController` was misleadingly named as it handled more than just HTTP concerns
- **Mixed responsibilities**: Single controller handled server health, connection management, AND validation operations
- **Violation of Single Responsibility Principle**: Made code harder to maintain and test

### Changes Made

#### 🏗️ **Controller Restructuring**
- **`ServerController`** - Handles general server health and information endpoints (`/api/status`, `/`)
- **`ConnectionController`** - Manages WebSocket connection endpoints (`/api/connections/*`)

## Summary

Fixes critical release automation workflow failures caused by version conflicts between GitHub Actions workflow and Makefile build system.

**Addresses Issue #48**: Release/Tagging Automation Workflow Failing

## Root Cause Analysis

The release workflow was failing due to version extraction inconsistencies:

author: carlosalaniz
body:
**refactor(frontend):** Replace string-based `ConfigKeys` with a strict union type and update usages
**fix(frontend):** Ensure Vite CSR builds correctly receive env variables via `import.meta.env`

* Defined `ConfigKeys` as a strict union type (no more string fallback).
* Added `clientBuildEnv` with all keys from `ConfigKeys`, populated via `import.meta.env`.
* Updated `getConfig()` to resolve environment variables in the following order:

  * `process.env` during SSR
  * `window.hievents` when injected
  * `clientBuildEnv` during CSR
  * a provided fallback

---

Prior to this change, the app relied on `window.hievents` to access environment variables at runtime. That worked fine for SSR deployments (which most of ours are), since the server injects `window.hievents` into the rendered HTML.

However, in CSR builds, environment variables like `import.meta.env.VITE_*` are injected **at build time** and are not preserved in the runtime global scope (i.e., not available on `window`). This caused CSR builds to silently break — wrong base URLs, missing logos, broken colors, and failing third-party integrations.

This update ensures that both SSR and CSR builds correctly load the expected environment config, restoring reliability and consistency across deployment types.

author: carrino
body:
Implemented long polling for the TechDisc integration and refined data handling:

- Changed the update interval to 1 second to allow the coordinator to quickly re-establish a connection.
- Increased the API call timeout to 60 seconds to enable long polling.
- Modified data processing to robustly distinguish between actual new throw data and server timeout signals (200 OK with minimal payload).
  - Only payloads with a valid `throwTime` object (containing `_seconds` and `_nanoseconds`) are treated as new data.
  - If a minimal payload is received (indicating no new throw from the server):
    - Existing sensor data is maintained if available.
    - `UpdateFailed` is raised if no prior data exists (e.g., on startup), preventing errors from processing incomplete data.
  - Client-side timeouts and API errors also correctly result in `UpdateFailed`.

This ensures sensors update promptly with new throws while correctly handling various timeout and error scenarios inherent in long polling.

### Release Notes

<summary>getsentry/sentry-go (github.com/getsentry/sentry-go)</summary>

### [`v0.34.0`](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/releases/tag/v0.34.0): 0.34.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/compare/v0.33.0...v0.34.0)

The Sentry SDK team is happy to announce the immediate availability of Sentry Go SDK v0.34.0.

##### Breaking Changes

-   Logrus structured logging support replaces the `sentrylogrus.Hook` signature from a `*Hook` to an interface.

```go
var hook *sentrylogrus.Hook
hook = sentrylogrus.New(
    // ... your setup
)

// should change the definition to 
var hook sentrylogrus.Hook
hook = sentrylogrus.New(
    // ... your setup
)
```

##### Features

-   Structured logging support for [slog](https://pkg.go.dev/log/slog). ([#​1033](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1033))

```go
ctx := context.Background()
handler := sentryslog.Option{
    EventLevel: []slog.Level{slog.LevelError, sentryslog.LevelFatal}, // Only Error and Fatal as events
    LogLevel:   []slog.Level{slog.LevelWarn, slog.LevelInfo},         // Only Warn and Info as logs
}.NewSentryHandler(ctx)
logger := slog.New(handler)
logger.Info("hello"))
```

-   Structured logging support for [logrus](https://redirect.github.com/sirupsen/logrus). ([#​1036](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1036))

```go
logHook, _ := sentrylogrus.NewLogHook(
    []logrus.Level{logrus.InfoLevel, logrus.WarnLevel}, 
    sentry.ClientOptions{
        Dsn: "your-dsn",
        EnableLogs: true, // Required for log entries    
    })
defer logHook.Flush(5 * time.Secod)
logrus.RegisterExitHandler(func() {
    logHook.Flush(5 * time.Second)
})

logger := logrus.New()
logger.AddHook(logHook)
logger.Infof("hello")
```

-   Add support for flushing events with context using `FlushWithContext()`. ([#​935](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/935))

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()

if !sentry.FlushWithContext(ctx) {
    // Handle timeout or cancellation
}
```

-   Add support for custom fingerprints in slog integration. ([#​1039](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1039))

##### Deprecations

-   Slog structured logging support replaces `Level` option with `EventLevel` and `LogLevel` options, for specifying fine-grained levels for capturing events and logs.

```go
handler := sentryslog.Option{
    EventLevel: []slog.Level{slog.LevelWarn, slog.LevelError, sentryslog.LevelFatal},
    LogLevel:   []slog.Level{slog.LevelDebug, slog.LevelInfo, slog.LevelWarn, slog.LevelError, sentryslog.LevelFatal},
}.NewSentryHandler(ctx)
```

-   Logrus structured logging support replaces `New` and `NewFromClient` functions to `NewEventHook`, `NewEventHookFromClient`, to match the newly added `NewLogHook` functions, and specify the hook type being created each time.

```go
logHook, err := sentrylogrus.NewLogHook(
    []logrus.Level{logrus.InfoLevel},
    sentry.ClientOptions{})
eventHook, err := sentrylogrus.NewEventHook([]logrus.Level{
    logrus.ErrorLevel,
    logrus.FatalLevel,
    logrus.PanicLevel,
}, sentry.ClientOptions{})
```

##### Bug Fixes

-   Fix issue where `ContinueTrace()` would panic when `sentry-trace` header does not exist. ([#​1026](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1026))
-   Fix incorrect log level signature in structured logging. ([#​1034](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1034))
-   Remove `sentry.origin` attribute from Sentry logger to prevent confusion in spans. ([#​1038](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1038))
-   Don't gate user information behind `SendDefaultPII` flag for logs. ([#​1032](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1032))

##### Misc

-   Add more sensitive HTTP headers to the default list of headers that are scrubbed by default. ([#​1008](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/pull/1008))

### [`v0.33.0`](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/releases/tag/v0.33.0): 0.33.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/compare/v0.32.0...v0.33.0)

The Sentry SDK team is happy to announce the immediate availability of Sentry Go SDK v0.33.0.

##### Breaking Changes

-   Rename the internal `Logger` to `DebugLogger`. This feature was only used when you set `Debug: True` in your `sentry.Init()` call. If you haven't used the Logger directly, no changes are necessary. ([#​1012](https://redirect.github.com/getsentry/sentry-go/issues/1012))

##### Features

author: andriydev
body:
# Objective

- Pretty much all rendering stuff right now will do nothing if added before the RenderPlugin.
- Some of these cases also use `if let Some(render_app)` which adds a whole extra level of nesting.

## Solution

- Make them panic if there is no RenderApp! It is better to give a more immediate warning than your app just silently doing nothing. This also reduces nesting in some cases.
- One case is special (in `crates/bevy_render/src/lib.rs`): the `RenderPlugin` itself calls `initialize_render_app`, and then later checks if we have the `RenderApp`. By moving this `if` to the `initialize_render_app` function, we avoid the useless branch and the problem goes away!

- There are 4 remaining cases that I did not handle. I am willing to fix all in this PR if that's desired.
    - `bevy_text` adds an extraction schedule for extracting the text2d sprite to the rendering stuff. In theory though, a user could be using the `bevy_text` stack with their own rendering (so reusing the layout and stuff). This one I am the least confident about. I added a comment explaining this one.
    - `bevy_gizmos` prints a warning message about having the plugins in the wrong order. Since this is also messing with feature flags, I didn't feel compelled to mess with it.
    - `bevy_render` `ExtractResourcePlugin` prints a warning message about having the plugins in the wrong order. Since this plugin is intended to be added by users, and we already have a message, I decided to leave this alone.
    - `bevy_sprite::SpritePlugin` may be added even in headless situations (e.g., to register the `Sprite` type for spawning scenes). I added a comment explaining this one too.

---

I don't think this needs a migration guide, since no one should be depending on this - the plugins would pretty much do nothing before anyway.

* Added the `gorm.io/gorm/clause` package to the import statements in `category.go`, `menu.go`, and `table.go` to support the `OnConflict` functionality. Issue Number 🔢

#182

Issue Description 🛠️

This pull request implements the <ValidateUniqueIdInput /> reusable component, which fulfills the following requirements described in Issue #182:

  • Accepts student unique ID input.

  • Performs internal async validation by hitting an endpoint: /api/Students/{uniqueId}.

  • Returns validation status (true/false) to the parent via a getValidationStatus callback.

  • Shows validation feedback (success or error message) directly above the input field.

  • Internally handles debouncing, loading state, and UI flexibility.

  • Does not rely on external validation functions (isValidate).

💡 What Problem Does This Solve?

Before this component, validation had to be handled manually or externally in parent components. This PR simplifies that process by:

  • Abstracting the entire validation workflow into one clean, reusable component.

  • Making it easier for devs to drop in a working input field with validation logic already wired up.

  • Enabling consistent async validation UX across the app.

Additional Information (Optional) ℹ️

  • The API call uses fetch and expects the student object in the response for a valid ID.

  • The component includes built-in support for styling via props like width, height, and className.

  • Debounce delay is currently set to 600ms.

No breaking changes were introduced. Component is self-contained.

body:
This pull request is an experiment by Claude Code to add new features.

- [x] setup Claude Code __without CLAUDE.md__
- [x] run `claude`
- [x] send a prompt for adding `GetAs` generics support function
- [x] [request a review](https://github.com/goldeneggg/structil/pull/44#issuecomment-3016359757) after implementation

## Summary

I used the prompt (in Japanese) as follows:

```
あなたはGo言語およびプログラミング言語の型に関するスペシャリストです。

あなたにはgetter.goに実装されているGetter型に、ジェネリクスを活用した汎用的なメソッド `GetAs` を実装してもらいます。

Getter型には、structの各フィールドにフィールド名指定でアクセスする処理が型単位で提供されています。
このリポジトリはGo1.19に準拠していてジェネリクスを使用できる状況にある為、今後はジェネリクスを活用した汎用的なメソッド `GetAs` を提供することとして、現在型単位で提供されているメソッドをいずれ廃止したいと考えています。

まずは現状のGettetの実装を読み込んで仕様を理解し、同じ仕様をジェネリクス活用して完璧に実現する為の `GetAs` メソッドを実装してください。また、getter_test.goに`GetAs`メソッドに関する網羅性が高いテストコードも追加してください。実装が完了したら、あなたの成果の解説をGETTER_GENERICS.mdに記載してください。

実装にあたって不明点があれば、適宜私に確認をしてください。
```

__This prompt intentionally ignores the restriction that Go generics cannot define type parameters in method definitions.__
The purpose of this pull request is to verify how Claude Code behaves in response to such prompts.

In conclusion, __Claude Code generated code that initially violated the language specification. They realized the violation when they added tests and ran the tests, and started to recover.__

This pull request contains the final "working" artifact.

author: getreuer
body:
This PR integrates support for QMK's [Repeat Key](https://docs.qmk.fm/features/repeat_key) feature and its companion Alt Repeat Key into vial-qmk.

This firmware change corresponds to

* GUI: https://github.com/vial-kb/vial-gui/pull/334
* Docs: https://github.com/vial-kb/vial-kb.github.io/pull/64

The Alt Repeat Key is useful to implement a "magic key" aka "adaptive key" whose behavior depends on the last pressed key. To gain the full potential of this feature, Alt Repeat Key is made dynamically configurable for Vial to specify entries of the form `(last_keycode, alt_keycode)` (plus additional options) to say that when `last_keycode` was pressed, the Alt Repeat Key behaves as `alt_keycode`.

Details:
* Added `REPEAT_KEY_ENABLE ?= yes` in build_vial.mk.
* Following the Key Overrides implementation, added an EEPROM memory area, get/set message handlers, and helper functions to configure Alt Repeat Key entries.
* Set `msg[3] = VIAL_ALT_REPEAT_KEY_ENTRIES` in `dynamic_vial_get_number_of_entries`.
* The logic for Alt Repeat Key hooks into QMK core in vial.c in `get_alt_repeat_key_keycode_user()`.

author: kumanoryo
body:
## Summary
devcontainer.jsonで`containerEnv`による変数定義でエラーが発生する問題を修正し、`localEnv:USER`を使用してより確実に動作する設定に変更しました。

## 問題
以前の設定では`containerEnv`を使用していましたが、Remote Container実行時にエラーが発生することが判明：

```json
"containerEnv": {
    "DEVCONTAINER_USER": "devuser"
},
"remoteUser": "${containerEnv:DEVCONTAINER_USER}"
```

## 解決方法
ホストの環境変数を直接参照する`localEnv:USER`を使用：

```json
"remoteUser": "${localEnv:USER}",
"mounts": [
    "source=...,target=/home/${localEnv:USER}/...,..."
]
```

## 変更内容
1. **containerEnvセクションを削除**
   - 変数定義が不要になる
   - エラーの原因を排除

2. **localEnv:USERの使用**
   - `remoteUser`: ホストのユーザー名を自動取得
   - `mounts`: すべてのマウントパスで使用

## 効果
- **動作の安定性**: エラーが発生しない確実な設定
- **汎用性**: 各ユーザーの環境に自動適応
- **シンプル性**: 追加設定が不要

## 動作確認済み
- VS Code Remote Containers拡張での動作を確認
- 他の環境でも正常に動作することを確認

- [x] VS Code Remote Containersで正常に起動すること
- [x] マウントボリュームが正しく設定されること
- [x] ユーザー権限が適切に設定されること

<!-- Discuss how this would affect game balance or explain why it was changed. Link any relevant discussions or issues. -->

As a solution I have made SS14.Labeller, a NativeAOT ASP NET Core application that labels PRs and issues using a webhook and GitHub PAT Token. Because it uses NativeAOT compilation, the application only uses around 20mb of RAM.

author: k1low
body:
This pull request introduces a caching mechanism for image objects to improve performance and reduce redundant processing. The key changes include the addition of a global cache in `cache.go`, modifications to the `Image` struct to include a `modTime` field, and updates to the `NewImage` function in `slide.go` to leverage the cache.

### Caching Mechanism:

* **Global Cache Implementation**: Added a thread-safe global cache in `cache.go` to store and retrieve `Image` objects based on a key. Includes `LoadImageCache` and `StoreImageCache` functions for accessing and updating the cache.

### Updates to `Image` Struct:

* **`modTime` Field**: Added a `modTime` field to the `Image` struct in `slide.go` to track the modification time of image files, enabling more precise cache validation.

### Enhancements to `NewImage` Function:

* **Cache Lookup for URLs**: Modified `NewImage` to check the cache for images fetched from URLs and return cached objects if available.
* **Cache Validation for Files**: Enhanced `NewImage` to validate cached images for local files using the `modTime` field, ensuring the cached version matches the file's modification time.
* **Cache Updates**: Updated `NewImage` to store newly created `Image` objects in the cache after processing.

## Description

Update the way cached makefile metadata are cached.\ 
Up until now, a single cache item (7s TTL) was generated whatever makefile was used.\

This new implementation allows generating a cache item per makefile path + content pair; allowing to get rid of the TTL. 

One may enable the new strategy by setting the following prior to source fast-synthax-highlighting

```sh
typeset -gA FAST_HIGHLIGHT
FAST_HIGHLIGHT[chroma-make-cache-global]=1
```

author: harshith-vaddiparthy
body:
## Problem
Currently, the Airweave platform lacks consistent input validation, which could lead to security vulnerabilities, inconsistent data, and potential application errors, especially when handling sensitive data like API keys, private keys, and OAuth2 tokens.

## Root Cause
The existing implementation:
- Has limited validation for input data, often relying on Pydantic alone
- Lacks consistent security checks for potentially malicious inputs
- Does not sanitize inputs to ensure consistent formatting
- Has no centralized validation system for similar input types

## Solution
This PR implements a comprehensive input validation system:

### 1. Flexible Validation Framework
- Created a modular validation framework in `utils/input_validation.py`
- Implemented validation for common data types: UUIDs, emails, URLs, datetimes, etc.
- Added specialized validation for security-sensitive inputs: API keys, auth codes, JWTs

### 2. Enhanced Security Checks
- Added pattern matching to detect SQL injection attempts
- Implemented XSS detection to prevent script injection
- Added command injection detection to protect against shell command execution
- Created a monitoring system to log potential security threats

### 3. Input Sanitization
- Added string sanitization methods (strip, trim, lowercase, etc.)
- Implemented consistent formatting for standardized inputs
- Added validation rule options for input transformation

### 4. OAuth2 Token Validation
- Enhanced OAuth2 token validation to ensure proper format and contents
- Added explicit validation of token responses
- Improved error handling and security logging

### 5. Testing and Documentation
- Added comprehensive unit tests for all validation functions
- Created predefined validation rule sets for common inputs
- Documented validation patterns for developer reference

## Testing
- Added 40+ unit tests for validation functions
- Tested with various input formats, both valid and invalid
- Verified security validation catches common attack patterns
- Confirmed backward compatibility with existing endpoints

## Benefits
1. **Enhanced Security**: Prevents malicious inputs through comprehensive validation
2. **Improved Data Quality**: Ensures consistent data formatting and validation
3. **Better Error Handling**: Provides clear, user-friendly validation error messages
4. **Centralized Logic**: Avoids scattered validation code with a unified approach
5. **Maintainability**: Makes adding new validation rules simple and consistent

## Potential Impact
This improvement enhances security and reliability without breaking existing functionality. The validation functions are designed to be used incrementally, allowing gradual adoption across the codebase.

body:
This pull request introduces a new Rust-based backend service, `milky-blog-service`, replacing the existing Python-based implementation. The changes include setting up the project's dependencies, Docker configuration, database migrations, and API documentation. Below is a summary of the most important changes grouped by theme:

### Project Setup and Dependencies
* Added `Cargo.toml` with dependencies for web framework (`actix-web`), database (`sqlx`), AWS SDK, and other utilities for the Rust-based service.

### Docker and Build Configuration
* Replaced the Python-based `Dockerfile` with a Rust-based build process, including caching dependencies and compiling the `milky-blog-service` binary.
* Added `docker-compose.yml` to define services for the blog, PostgreSQL, MinIO (S3-compatible storage), and Consul for service discovery and configuration.

### Database Migrations
* Created initial SQL migrations (`20250620180415_init.up.sql` and `20250620180415_init.down.sql`) to define tables for articles, tags, comments, and associated relationships. Includes triggers and functions for cleaning unused tags. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-32b0b7ae38600cca6757f871bc1f2f36544af1bcb96dd7307f9371b95492ca74R1-R118) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bcc87d2691a4d1ddc7d27067527fa8d7072065b53be41532d0737e60678dfc94R1-R17)
* Added `Makefile` targets for managing database migrations using `sqlx`.

### API Documentation
* Introduced OpenAPI documentation (`docs/openapi.json`) for the `milky-blog-service` API, detailing endpoints for managing articles, files, and comments.

### Miscellaneous
* Removed the obsolete `alembic.ini` file used for Python-based database migrations.
* Added a minimal `build.rs` file for the Rust project setup.
* Updated `README.md` with environment variables, Consul configuration examples, and instructions for running the service manually or via Docker Compose.

author: stormcat24
body:
## Summary
- Automatically deploy LocalStack when creating a new ECS cluster if `KECS_LOCALSTACK_ENABLED=true`
- Each k3d cluster gets its own LocalStack instance for AWS service emulation
- LocalStack pods persist when KECS is restarted with `KECS_KEEP_CLUSTERS_ON_SHUTDOWN=true`

## Changes
- Add LocalStack manager to DefaultECSAPI
- Implement `deployLocalStackIfEnabled` method that deploys LocalStack after cluster creation
- Add environment variable binding for `KECS_LOCALSTACK_ENABLED`
- Use cluster-specific Kubernetes client for LocalStack deployment

## Testing
1. Start KECS with LocalStack enabled:
   ```bash
   KECS_SECURITY_ACKNOWLEDGED=true KECS_LOCALSTACK_ENABLED=true ./bin/kecs server
   ```

2. Create a new cluster:
   ```bash
   aws --endpoint-url http://localhost:8080 ecs create-cluster --cluster-name test-cluster
   ```

3. Verify LocalStack is running:
   ```bash
   docker exec k3d-kecs-test-cluster-server-0 kubectl get pods -n aws-services
   ```

## Known Issues
- LocalStack deployment state is not tracked in storage, so KECS doesn't remember which clusters have LocalStack deployed after restart
- Health check fails with DNS resolution errors when checking from outside the cluster, but LocalStack works correctly within the cluster

These issues will be addressed in a follow-up PR.

author: samitouil
body:
## Overview

This PR fixes a critical bug in the week template export/import system where the `applyRule` property (and other important properties) were being lost during the import process.

## Problem

The week template seeding in `backend/src/prisma/seed.ts` was missing several critical properties:
- `applyRule`: Determines when templates should be automatically applied (EVEN_WEEKS, ODD_WEEKS, etc.)
- `isDefault`: Marks templates as default
- `priority`: Controls template application order

Additionally, the export script was missing week template related data entirely.

## Solution

### Export Script Enhancements (`backend/scripts/export-db.ts`)
- Added `weekTemplates`, `weekTemplateDays`, `weekOverrides`, `taskOverrides` to DbExport interface
- Added corresponding Prisma queries to export all week template related data
- Enhanced logging to show counts for exported week template data

### Import Script Fixes (`backend/src/prisma/seed.ts`)
- Added missing properties to week template seeding:
  - `isDefault: templateData.isDefault`
  - `applyRule: templateData.applyRule`
  - `priority: templateData.priority`

## Testing

### Before Fix
- Week templates had null `applyRule` values after import
- Export script was missing week template data
- `npm run db:safe-push` would lose week template configuration

### After Fix
- ✅ Export correctly captures: `"applyRule": "EVEN_WEEKS"` and `"applyRule": "ODD_WEEKS"`
- ✅ Import correctly preserves: `applyRule=EVEN_WEEKS, isDefault=false, priority=0`
- ✅ Complete export/import cycle maintains all week template properties
- ✅ All backend unit tests passing (142 passed, 4 skipped)
- ✅ All frontend unit tests passing (154 passed, 1 skipped)

## Impact

This fix ensures that:
1. Week templates maintain their automatic application rules through database updates
2. The `npm run db:safe-push` workflow preserves all week template configuration
3. Manual routine application functionality continues to work correctly
4. Database schema updates don't lose critical week template metadata

## Files Changed

- `backend/scripts/export-db.ts`: Added week template data export
- `backend/src/prisma/seed.ts`: Fixed week template property preservation

## Related

This fix supports the "Apply Weekly Routine" functionality implemented in PR #77 by ensuring that week templates and their rules are properly preserved through database operations.

body:
<!--
Please describe the pull request motivation and changes here along with non-obvious things.
-->
This PR adds support for JSON-schema generation support via `schemars` for all types that implement the `serde` traits. JSON-schema can give config files a schema for validation and assistance in text editor environments. At a minimum `schemars` v1.0.3 (versus just `v1` like serde) is required to support rust edition 2018.

To avoid increasing the MSRV unduly, I amended the MSRV check to restrict itself to default features and ensured the feature is enabled in regular CI checks.

With the upgrade to schemars 1.0 map keys as used in starship are required to implement the `JsonSchema` trait instead of it assuming string keys. If this feature is not acceptable this could be worked around in starship, but eventually having a schema for `os_info` types in the starship config schema (the extra information is not used by `schemars` yet) would be nice to have.

author: copilot
body:
When Markdown format checking fails and the `--debug` flag is used, the debug output was truncating chunk content at 150 characters, making it impossible to properly debug format validation issues.

## Problem

Users would see truncated output like this:
```
--- 區塊 1 ---
原始: # Test Document for Debug Issue\n\nThis is a test document that contains very long content to trigger the truncation issue in debug mode. The content ...
翻譯: # 除錯問題測試文件\n\n這是包含很長內容的測試文件，目的是觸發除錯模式中的截斷問題。內容應該足夠長，超過150個字符，這樣我們可以看到截斷的情況。\n\n## 長內容部分\n\n- 這是一個非常長的列表項目，包含大量文本，絕對應該超過目前在showMarkdownFormatDebug函數中應用...
```

The truncation made it impossible to see the complete chunk content needed for debugging format inconsistencies.

## Solution

Modified the `showMarkdownFormatDebug` function in `main.js` to remove the 150-character truncation limit:

**Before:**
```javascript
console.error(`原始: ${originalText.replace(/\n/g, '\\n').substring(0, 150)}${originalText.length > 150 ? '...' : ''}`);
```

**After:**
```javascript
console.error(`原始: ${originalText.replace(/\n/g, '\\n')}`);
```

## Changes Made

- Removed `.substring(0, 150)` truncation logic from lines 603 and 610 in `main.js`
- Removed ellipsis indicators (`${text.length > 150 ? '...' : ''}`)
- Added comprehensive test case to prevent regression
- All existing functionality remains unchanged

## Result

Users now see complete chunk content when using `--debug`:
```
--- 區塊 1 ---
原始: # Test Document for Debug Issue\n\nThis is a test document that contains very long content to trigger the truncation issue in debug mode. The content should be long enough to exceed 150 characters so we can see the truncation happening.\n\n## Section with Long Content\n\n- This is a very long list item that contains a lot of text and should definitely exceed the 150 character limit that is currently being applied in the showMarkdownFormatDebug function.
翻譯: # 除錯問題測試文件\n\n這是包含很長內容的測試文件，目的是觸發除錯模式中的截斷問題。內容應該足夠長，超過150個字符，這樣我們可以看到截斷的情況。\n\n## 長內容部分\n\n- 這是一個非常長的列表項目，包含大量文本，絕對應該超過目前在showMarkdownFormatDebug函數中應用的150個字符限制。
```

This enables proper debugging of Markdown format validation issues by providing complete visibility into chunk content.

Fixes #28.

# 🚀 풀 리퀘스트 제안

<!-- 이슈 지울때 작성해 주세요. -->
<!-- closes #issue-number -->
<!-- 이슈 여러 개 일 경우, closes #1, closes #2 -->
<!-- https://docs.github.com/ko/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->

## 📋 작업 내용
### 프로젝트 구조 변경 목표
- `api/profile/get/route.ts`: 특정 사용자의 프로필 정보를 가져오는 API Route (GET 요청 처리)
- `api/profile/update/route.ts`: 특정 사용자의 프로필 정보를 업데이트하는 API Route (POST 요청 처리)
- `features/profile/api/getProfile.ts`: /api/profile/get API Route를 호출하는 queryFn
- `features/profile/api/updateProfile.ts`:  /api/profile/update API Route를 호출하는 mutationFn

```
├── app/
│   ├── api/
│   │   └── profile/
│   │       ├── get/
│   │       │   └── route.ts         // 프로필 조회 API Route (GET)
│   │       └── update/
│   │           └── route.ts       // 프로필 업데이트 API Route (POST)
│   └── profile/                 
│       └── page.tsx            
└── features/
    └── profile/
        └── api/
            ├── getProfile.ts     // 서버 컴포넌트에서 API Route 호출 (현재로서는 서버 전용)
            └── updateProfile.ts  // API Route 호출 (useMutation의 mutationFn)
```

## 🔧 변경 사항
**supabase 접근 방식 변경**
- 기존: 직접 supabase 인스턴스를 사용하여 데이터베이스에 접근.
- 변경: Next.js API route 를 통해 서버에서 Supabase에 접근. 
- 장점:
    - 보안 강화: Supabase API Key와 같은 민감한 정보가 클라이언트에 노출되지 않습니다. 모든 데이터베이스 작업은 서버에서 이루어집니다.
    - 인증 및 권한 관리 용이: API Route 내부에서 createRouteHandlerClient를 사용하여 세션 정보를 안전하게 가져와 사용자 인증 및 권한 확인 로직을 추가하기 용이합니다.
  - 로직 중앙화: 데이터베이스 관련 로직을 API Route에 집중시켜 관리 및 디버깅이 쉬워집니다.

**queryFn, mutationFn(fetch 함수) 분리**
기존: getProfile, updateProfile(update.ts에서 이름 변경) 함수가 직접 Supabase를 호출.

변경: `features/profile/api/getProfile.ts`, `features/profile/api/updateProfile.ts` 파일에서 API Route를 fetch하는 역할만 담당.

장점:
- 관심사 분리: 데이터베이스 접근 로직과 클라이언트에서 API를 호출하는 로직이 명확히 분리됩니다.
- 재사용성: 동일한 API Route를 여러 클라이언트 컴포넌트에서 쉽게 재사용할 수 있습니다.
- 테스트 용이성: 각 계층의 테스트를 독립적으로 수행하기 용이해집니다. 

```
// 이 함수는 서버 컴포넌트(pages.tsx)에서 직접 호출되어 사용자의 프로필을 가져옵니다.
// 따라서 NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL 환경 변수를 사용해 절대 경로로 API Route를 호출합니다.

import { UserProfileType } from '@/widgets/profile';

export const getProfile = async (userId: string): Promise<UserProfileType> => {
  const response = await fetch(
    // 서버에서 호출되므로 반드시 절대 경로 사용
    `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/api/profile/get?userId=${userId}`,
    {
      cache: 'no-store', // 또는 필요한 캐싱 전략
    }
  );

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorData = await response.json();
    throw new Error(errorData.message || 'Failed to fetch profile');
  }

  return response.json();
};

```

```
const Page = async () => {
...
  // getProfile 함수가 서버에서 호출됩니다.
  const userProfile = await getProfile(userData?.id!);

  return <ProfileForm user={userProfile} />
};
```

**env.local에 NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001 환경 변수 추가**
Next.js 서버 환경에서 fetch 함수를 사용할 때, `/api/profile/get`과 같이 상대 경로를 사용했습니다. 그런데 Failed to parse URL from /api/profile/get 에러가 발생하였습니다.

원인
Next.js 서버 환경에서 fetch 함수를 사용할 때 상대 경로는 현재 실행 중인 서버의 베이스 URL을 기준으로 해석될 수 없습니다. 웹 브라우저 환경에서는 브라우저가 현재 페이지의 URL을 기준으로 상대 경로를 자동으로 완성해주지만, Node.js 환경에서는 그렇지 않습니다.
따라서 절대 경로를 사용해야 합니다. 

해결
```
# .env.local

# 개발 환경에서는 Next.js 앱이 실행되는 로컬 주소 (일반적으로 3000번 포트)
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001

# 배포 환경에서는 실제 서비스 도메인
# 예: NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://your-app-domain.com
```

사용
```
const response = await fetch(`${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/api/profile/get?userId=${userData?.id!}`, {
      cache: 'no-store' // 또는 revalidatePath를 사용하여 캐시를 제어
    });
```

## Summary

This PR implements comprehensive OIDC authentication support for the Chefify application as outlined in issue #3. The implementation includes:

• **OIDC Configuration**: Added Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect package and configured authentication with cookie and OIDC schemes in Program.cs
• **Authentication Middleware**: Created custom AuthenticationMiddleware to process user claims after authentication
• **User Management**: Implemented IUserService interface and UserService for creating/retrieving users based on OIDC claims
• **Domain Models**: Added User entity with OIDC claim mapping (sub → ExternalId, email → Email, name → Name)
• **Configuration**: Added authentication settings to appsettings.json files with environment variable support
• **Authorization**: Added [Authorize] attribute to WeatherForecast endpoint for testing authentication flow
• **Testing**: Created integration tests to verify authentication configuration and service registration

## Technical Implementation

- **Authentication Flow**: Cookie authentication as default scheme with OIDC as challenge scheme
- **Claims Mapping**: Maps OIDC standard claims (sub, email, name) to User entity properties
- **Scopes**: Configured openid, profile, and email scopes for comprehensive user information
- **Environment Support**: Supports both development and production configurations
- **Error Handling**: Robust error handling in UserService with proper logging

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: stephenliang
body:
The middleware was copied from the vercel multi-tenant example which includes a tenant id matcher. However, it appears the example has a bug which matches paths such as `/a.b.c/xyz` which causes the locale not to be rendered and sets the locale as `a.b.c` which ends up throwing an error. Rather, the multi-tenancy works as expected without this Regex because we use `NextResponse.rewrite` which proxies[1] the branded request while preserving the original URL. In other words, currently a request to `/code.org/en-US/engineering/all-the-things` works (when it shouldn't), but the middleware using the rewrite proxy `/en-US/engineering/all-the-things` also works because it proxies the request internally.

This should fix some security robots throwing 500s in production.

[1] https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#rewrite

author: alexandre-bourdois
body:
# 🤖 Fix: Notifications Discord pour les PRs Dependabot

## 📌 Description

- **Contexte** : Les workflows GitHub Actions de notification Discord ne s'exécutent pas pour les PRs créées par Dependabot.
- **Problème résolu** : Les notifications Discord ne sont pas envoyées lorsque Dependabot crée des PRs ou demande des reviews automatiquement.
- **Solution apportée** : Modification des triggers des workflows pour utiliser `pull_request_target` au lieu de `pull_request` et ajout de la détection spécifique de Dependabot.

## ✅ Type de changement

Cochez les options pertinentes :

- [x] 🐛 Correction de bug
- [ ] ✨ Nouvelle fonctionnalité
- [ ] 🔧 Refactoring
- [ ] 📝 Mise à jour de la documentation
- [ ] 🚀 Amélioration des performances
- [ ] ✅ Ajout de tests
- [ ] 🔒 Amélioration de la sécurité
- [ ] Autre (précisez) :

## 🔍 Comment tester cette PR ?

Fournissez des instructions pour tester les modifications :

1. Fusionner cette PR
2. Attendre qu'une PR Dependabot soit créée automatiquement (ou déclencher manuellement une mise à jour des dépendances)
3. Vérifier que les notifications Discord sont bien envoyées sur les canaux configurés
4. Vérifier que les messages distinguent bien les PRs Dependabot (emoji 🤖) des PRs normales

## 📎 Liens associés

- **Issues liées** : Référence à l'issue du bug des notifications Discord Dependabot
- **Documentation** : [GitHub Actions pull_request_target documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull_request_target)
- **Autres PRs** : Aucune

## 👥 Revue

- **Relecteurs suggérés** : @AlexLakarm @pylejeune
- **Domaines concernés** : GitHub Actions workflows, intégrations Discord, configuration Dependabot

## 🧪 Checklist

- [x] Le code compile sans erreur
- [x] Les tests unitaires passent (N/A pour les workflows)
- [x] La documentation est à jour
- [x] Les dépendances sont à jour
- [x] La PR est prête pour la revue

## 🔧 Détails techniques

### Modifications apportées :

**`.github/workflows/notify-discord-pr.yml`** :

- Remplacement de `pull_request:` par `pull_request_target:`
- Ajout de la détection automatique de Dependabot avec `github.actor == "dependabot[bot]"`
- Messages différenciés avec emoji 🤖 pour les PRs Dependabot

**`.github/workflows/notify-reviewers-discord.yml`** :

- Remplacement de `pull_request:` par `pull_request_target:`
- Amélioration du message avec le titre de la PR et l'URL
- Gestion spécifique des notifications de review pour Dependabot

### Pourquoi `pull_request_target` ?

GitHub Actions utilise des restrictions de sécurité pour les PRs créées par des bots comme Dependabot. Le trigger `pull_request` n'a pas accès aux secrets pour ces PRs, tandis que `pull_request_target` s'exécute dans le contexte de la branche de base avec les permissions complètes.

## 🗒️ Notes complémentaires

- Cette correction permettra de recevoir toutes les notifications Discord, y compris pour les mises à jour automatiques des dépendances
- Les messages Discord incluront maintenant des icônes distinctives pour identifier facilement les PRs Dependabot
- Aucun impact sur les PRs créées par des utilisateurs normaux - elles continueront de fonctionner comme avant

author: taisgb
body:
# Feature: Implementa Estrutura Base da API com Módulos de Usuários, Itens e Propostas

## Contexto

Esta Pull Request estabelece a estrutura inicial e modular da API para o projeto `Projeto_AvantiBootcamp`. O objetivo é fornecer uma base robusta e organizada para o desenvolvimento das funcionalidades de gerenciamento de usuários, itens e propostas, seguindo as boas práticas de arquitetura de software (MVC/Camadas de Serviço e Repositório).

## Alterações Realizadas

Foram criados os seguintes módulos e seus respectivos componentes, seguindo a estrutura de `controllers`, `repositories`, `routes` e `services` para cada entidade principal:

### 1. Módulo de Usuários
* **`usuarios.controller.js`**: Lógica de manipulação de requisições e respostas para usuários (e.g., criação, busca).
* **`usuarios.repository.js`**: Abstração da camada de acesso a dados para a entidade `Usuário`, utilizando o Prisma Client.
* **`usuarios.routes.js`**: Definição das rotas específicas para `Usuários` (e.g., `/api/usuarios`, `/api/usuarios/:id`).
* **`usuarios.service.js`**: Lógica de negócio e coordenação entre controller e repository para `Usuário`.

### 2. Módulo de Itens
* **`itens.controller.js`**: Lógica de manipulação de requisições e respostas para itens.
* **`itens.repository.js`**: Abstração da camada de acesso a dados para a entidade `Item`.
* **`itens.routes.js`**: Definição das rotas específicas para `Itens` (e.g., `/api/itens`).
* **`itens.service.js`**: Lógica de negócio e coordenação para `Item`.

### 3. Módulo de Propostas
* **`proposta.controller.js`**: Lógica de manipulação de requisições e respostas para propostas.
* **`proposta.repository.js`**: Abstração da camada de acesso a dados para a entidade `Proposta`.
* **`proposta.routes.js`**: Definição das rotas específicas para `Propostas` (e.g., `/api/propostas`).
* **`proposta.service.js`**: Lógica de negócio e coordenação para `Proposta`.

### Outras Alterações:
* **`src/routes/index.js`**: Centralização das rotas, integrando os módulos de `usuários`, `itens` e `propostas` sob os respectivos prefixos (`/api/usuarios`, `/api/itens`, `/api/propostas`).
* **`src/prisma/client.js`**: Configuração do Prisma Client para conexão com o banco de dados.
* **Estrutura de Pastas**: Organização do projeto em `controllers`, `repositories`, `routes` e `services` dentro de `src` para promover a modularidade e a manutenibilidade.

## Como Testar (Exemplos Iniciais - Adapte conforme a implementação):

1.  Garanta que o banco de dados esteja configurado e o `prisma migrate dev` (ou similar) tenha sido executado.
2.  Inicie a aplicação (ex: `npm start` ou `node index.js`).
3.  **Para Usuários:**
    * `POST /api/usuarios`: Tente criar um novo usuário com os campos necessários (ex: `nome`, `email`, `senha`).
    * `GET /api/usuarios`: Verifique se é possível listar usuários.
    * `GET /api/usuarios/:id`: Verifique se é possível obter um usuário por ID.
4.  **Para Itens:**
    * `POST /api/itens`: Tente criar um novo item.
    * `GET /api/itens`: Verifique se é possível listar itens.
5.  **Para Propostas:**
    * `POST /api/propostas`: Tente criar uma nova proposta.
    * `GET /api/propostas`: Verifique se é possível listar propostas.

## Observações / Próximos Passos:

* Esta PR foca na **estrutura e integração inicial** dos módulos.
* Validações mais complexas, tratamento robusto de erros e autenticação/autorização serão implementados em PRs futuras (se ainda não estiverem aqui).

This commit updates various dependencies to their latest versions, including Kotlin, Android Gradle Plugin, Compose, Ktor, and others.

It also replaces the usage of `kotlinx.datetime.Clock` with `kotlin.time.Clock` and `kotlinx.datetime.Instant` with `kotlin.time.Instant` for time-related operations. Additionally, it updates the usage of `monthNumber` and `dayOfMonth` from `kotlinx.datetime.LocalDateTime` to `month.number` and `day` respectively.

A workaround for a Ktor R8/ProGuard issue has been added by introducing `FieldSkippingClassVisitor` to strip fields from `io.ktor.client.plugins.Messages` during transformation.

The `core/common` module's dependencies were streamlined, and the `core-base/datastore` module now directly depends on `kotlinx-datetime`.

author: tonestone57
body:
Further refines the Haiku OS benchmark porting:

1.  **No `mallinfo` in `xmalloc-test.c`**:
    *   Previous assessment was incorrect; `xmalloc-test.c` does not use `mallinfo()`. No changes were needed in this file regarding `mallinfo`.

2.  **Exclude `glibc-bench` for Haiku**:
    *   The `glibc-simple` and `glibc-thread` benchmarks are now conditionally excluded from the build when targeting Haiku OS.
    *   These benchmarks appear tightly coupled with GNU C Library internals (t-cache, fastbins) and its specific benchmarking framework. Adapting them for Haiku would likely be a significant effort and is deferred from this initial port.
    *   Modified `bench/CMakeLists.txt` to wrap the `add_executable` calls for these benchmarks in an `if(NOT HAIKU)` block.

This commit streamlines the initial Haiku port by focusing on benchmarks that are more readily compatible or require less OS-specific adaptation.

## About the PR
This PR introduces balance changes by increasing the minimum player count (`minPlayers`) for most antagonist roles. It also removes some "meme" content, specifically fart-related emotes and sounds, and updates some posters and role requirements.

## Why / Balance
Increasing the `minPlayers` for antagonist modes like Nukeops, Traitor, Cult, and Wizard is an important balancing change. It ensures that intense and potentially round-disruptive roles only appear when there are enough players on the server to create an interesting and balanced gameplay experience. On low-population servers, these modes often lead to a quick and uninteresting end to the round.

The removal of the fart-related content is an effort to clean up and adjust the overall tone of the game.

## Technical details
- Changed the `minPlayers` value in many `.yml` files in `Resources/Prototypes/GameRules/`, `Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/GameRules/`, and others.
- Commented out or removed the `Fart` component and related definitions in `Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Mobs/base.yml`, `Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/SoundCollections/emotes.yml`, and `Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/Voice/speech_emotes.yml`.
- Updated a poster definition in `Resources/Prototypes/Entities/Structures/Wallmounts/Signs/posters.yml`.
- Commented out the requirements for the Passenger role in `Resources/Prototypes/Roles/Jobs/Civilian/assistant.yml`.
- Commented out the `ImmovableRodSkibidi` variant in `Resources/Prototypes/_Goobstation/Entities/Objects/Fun/immovable_rod.yml`.

author: raythurnvoid
body:
Fixes: https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/16114

When a `$state` or a `$derived` is directly set by the user, we properly add it to the `old_values` `Map`.

However when a derived is updated as a result of the `check_dirtiness` check during `flush_queued_effects`, we do not save the old value, hence the value read in a teardown function of a `$effect` is not the old value but the new one, this is incosistent with the "old value behavior" that was recently introduced.

In this PR i save the old value when the `$derived` is updated, so that it will be used by teardown functions of `$effect`s.

However while working on this i've noticed that there's an edge case when working with child components.

While passing a prop in certain conditions (either a legacy bindable or a prop accessed via `$.prop` because it has a setter somewhere in the code) the original `$state` is wrapped in a `derived`. When the child component is destroyed the teardown functions might read `$.prop` values that did not got update because thay were not read (perhaps in the template). This means that is possible that during the execution of the teardown the values of the derived are either `null` because they were never initialized because nothing ever read from it, or they are outdated. I've opened a separate issue for this: https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/16262.

This bug is present both before and after the changes of this PR.

This pull request introduces a new feature to support installing MCP server configurations via both commands and APIs, along with several related enhancements and adjustments. Below is a summary of the most important changes categorized by their themes:

### New MCP Configuration Feature:
* Added a new command, `agent-maestro.installMcpConfig`, to install MCP configurations through the VS Code extension. This includes a user-friendly interface to select supported extensions and handle configuration installation with progress reporting and error handling (`package.json`, `src/extension.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-04bba6a35cad1c794cbbe677678a51de13441b7a6ee8592b7b50be1f05c6f626R219-R303) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R109-R113).
* Introduced a new API endpoint, `POST /api/v1/roo/install-mcp-config`, to allow programmatic installation of MCP configurations, including validation of supported extensions and error handling (`src/server/routes/rooRoutes.ts`, [src/server/routes/rooRoutes.tsR770-R897](diffhunk://#diff-bc30e470b5656b3c242a07b912ad2630a3597c1f7c0fa4c21dfe2152464ef04aR770-R897)).

### Codebase Enhancements:
* Updated the `ProxyServer` and `registerRooRoutes` to pass the `vscode.ExtensionContext` for accessing global storage and other extension-specific resources (`src/server/ProxyServer.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ec34d12362a10b8031f6b09f0cf3e16b78ef6950705e5b72820390006b676151R16-R26) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ec34d12362a10b8031f6b09f0cf3e16b78ef6950705e5b72820390006b676151L173-R184); `src/server/routes/rooRoutes.ts`, [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-bc30e470b5656b3c242a07b912ad2630a3597c1f7c0fa4c21dfe2152464ef04aR139).
* Added new utility functions, `getAvailableExtensions` and `addAgentMaestroMcpConfig`, to handle MCP configuration logic (`src/extension.ts`, [src/extension.tsR7-R10](diffhunk://#diff-04bba6a35cad1c794cbbe677678a51de13441b7a6ee8592b7b50be1f05c6f626R7-R10)).

### Minor Adjustments:
* Renamed the MCP tool name from "Execute_Roo_Tasks" to "Execute Roo Tasks" for improved readability and consistency (`src/server/McpServer.ts`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d4755364acbf96cdec9c9a2191b167b661dd54f5ff4272b486a11e7ba1b6a09cL113-R113) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d4755364acbf96cdec9c9a2191b167b661dd54f5ff4272b486a11e7ba1b6a09cL124-R124) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d4755364acbf96cdec9c9a2191b167b661dd54f5ff4272b486a11e7ba1b6a09cL139-R146).
* Added a placeholder comment to include MCP server info in the global state in the future (`src/server/McpServer.ts`, [src/server/McpServer.tsR166-R167](diffhunk://#diff-d4755364acbf96cdec9c9a2191b167b661dd54f5ff4272b486a11e7ba1b6a09cR166-R167)). 

These changes collectively enhance the functionality and usability of the Agent Maestro extension, making it easier to manage MCP server configurations.
